purpose: Independent reproduction of the four-hourly publisher outage and line-by-line verification of what the deployed site actually shows. No probability, pick or alias is written by this session; every number below is either read from a repository artefact, re-derived from a cited official endpoint, or reproduced locally.

publisher_outage.summary: Four consecutive scheduled pages.yml runs failed at the same step, and the published site stayed on the 2026-10-23T20:10:00Z snapshot for 10.5 h (the repository's own stale_after_hours is 8).

publisher_outage.method: gh run view <id> --json jobs, which reports each job's conclusion and the names of its failed steps. The run log archive itself is hosted on productionresultssa19.blob.core.windows.net, which this sandbox cannot reach (HTTP 403 on the signed URL, curl exit 0 with an EOF body), so the failing test was identified by reproduction instead of by reading the log.

reproduction.tree: 2f966a91a103398c4ae5513828c81e32897f8af8 (the head of all four failing runs; checked out read-only into a separate git worktree)
reproduction.raised: scripts.root_publish.PublishRefused: snapshot 2026-10-23T09:23:57+00:00 is 21.3h old (limit 12.0h); pass --allow-stale to publish it anyway
reproduction.cause: tests/test_ca7e10e5_snapshot.py called scripts.root_publish.build_plan(self.output, self.root) without a reference clock, so the test compared the wall clock against a fixed 2026-10-23T09:23:57Z fixture. It passed for the first twelve hours after it was written and then failed permanently, which is why 2f966a9's first three scheduled runs (21:41, 23:08, 01:08) failed and every later run would have failed the same way.

fix_in_tree_and_verified_here.change: the three calls now pass now=datetime(2026, 10, 23, 10, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

guard_added_by_this_session.rule: no test module may call root_publish.build_plan() against a fixed fixture without pinning now= (a **splat whose dict pins now is accepted and asserted separately)
guard_added_by_this_session.proof_it_would_have_caught_the_outage: the same AST scan reports three unpinned calls at lines 73, 77 and 84 of the pre-fix 2f966a9 file and one pinned call in the fixed file

second_irregularity_push_runs_starved.observation: While other sessions pushed main roughly once a minute between 06:32Z and 06:44Z, pages.yml push runs 40070626757 (06:32:44Z), 40071009969 (06:38:38Z) and 40071346040 (06:43:44Z) were each cancelled while still pending, as the workflow's own concurrency comment documents. The scheduled slot at 06:47Z (cron '47 2-22/4 * * *') had not started by 06:53Z, and this session's token cannot create a workflow_dispatch run (HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration), so freshness could not be forced from here.
second_irregularity_push_runs_starved.effect: A merge to main does not reliably refresh the site while many sessions are pushing; the four-hourly schedule is the only dependable trigger.
second_irregularity_push_runs_starved.action: Reported here and on the Flagged for Review page. Not changed by this session: .github/workflows/** is shared scope and the concurrency design is deliberate (see the comment block in pages.yml).

limitations: The sandbox has no direct egress to hltv.org, polymarket.com, egamersworld.com, smarkets.com or the Actions log blob host; page reads were made through the agent's page-fetch proxy, which returns the rendered text/JSON of a URL but cannot write a byte-for-byte evidence copy into data/evidence/. Every re-read below therefore carries its endpoint and read time instead of a saved payload.

No live collection could be run from this sandbox, so the 'picks for every live card' claim can only be verified after the publisher completes a run; this session verified the mechanism and the published rows, not a fresh collection.

The four-hourly publisher could not be dispatched (HTTP 403) and its push-triggered runs were being cancelled while other sessions pushed main; the next scheduled slot at 06:47Z had not started by 06:53Z.
